summary: AgentHub is a clear Hub/Edge dual-plane system with shared React workbench surfaces (Desktop/Web/Mobile). Architecture seams and non-negotiable boundaries are well documented and largely reflected in code (platform adapters, Local Edge only on Desktop, Hub-only Web/Mobile). The main cleanup risks are narrative drift—especially production LIVE on hk3 vs CI/docs still saying decommissioned—plus stale deploy templates, image-name divergence, leftover `app/mobile` Tauri path, and residual Edge `internal/runners` compatibility package. Prefer incremental SSOT alignment and seam hardening over any rewrite.

summary: Edge Server runtime is adapter-driven: lifecycle.ProcessExecutor owns process/state, adapters only BuildCommand+ParseStream, and runners is a thin /v1/runners compatibility shell. Security delivery is only partial—AH-SR-046 dual-token exists for run-start but is incomplete, AH-SR-045 remote read scoping is owner-filter only, and AH-SR-049 Hub callbacks remain best-effort without outbox/idempotency/reconciliation. Cleanup should split god-files (handlers, process_executor, store, orchestrator) and extract durable callback/capability seams before deeper rewrites.

summary: Hub Server is a layered Go control plane (app → router → handler → service → repository/model + ws/cache) with generally unidirectional imports and strong auth-session boundaries (OIDC identity → Hub-local JWT session → RequireHubSession). The main cleanup pressure is not missing architecture but concentration of multi-concern logic in AgentService (dispatch/outbox/run-events/edge-callback), a giant flat service package, partial maturity of outbox/relay/remote targets, and dual OpenAPI surface (/v1 Edge + Hub /client|/web|/edge) with known path drift.

key_facts.claim: Intended dependency direction is unidirectional: app wires handlers/services; handler depends on service interfaces (mostly); service depends on repository/model/cache/ws; repository depends on model/config; model has no internal deps; middleware/ws stay low-level.

hotspots.why: Largest desktop API fork (~1854 LOC) with overlapping but non-identical methods vs web/shared; primary divergence source for types, task/team APIs, and auth/error handling.
hotspots.suggested_action: Treat shared hubClient as SSOT; make desktop thin re-export + desktop-only extensions; freeze new methods on desktop-only client.

hotspots.why: Near-duplicate of desktop hubClient (~1705 LOC) with Session type and method-set drift (e.g. task approvals/artifacts present on web path).
hotspots.suggested_action: Diff against shared + desktop; migrate web callers to shared client first, keep only web-specific transport/auth glue.

hotspots.why: Intended shared client (~1533 LOC) already used by mobile and some shared tests, but not by desktop/web product path; incomplete ownership.
hotspots.suggested_action: Complete method parity needed by Desktop/Web models; add contract tests for endpoint/method parity before deleting forks.

hotspots.why: Adapter mixes contract compliance with demo exports, optimistic Hub mutation cache writes, and demoRuntimeFallback; AH-SR-043 leakage surface.
hotspots.suggested_action: Split pure adapter ports from demo seeds and mutation helpers; gate demo fallback strictly by dataMode contract + auth.

hotspots.why: Platform constructor imports and exposes demo conversations/agents/transcript as defaults; conversations.list always demo; run path can demo-fallback.
hotspots.suggested_action: Keep demo only behind explicit mock/fixture options; real conversations should not live as module-level demo exports.

hotspots.why: Giant orphan (~2386 LOC) parallel to shared SettingsPage used by WorkbenchRoutes; high merge/confusion risk.
hotspots.suggested_action: Confirm no runtime import graph, then quarantine/delete after extracting any unique sections into shared or desktop settings adapters.

hotspots.why: Orphan settings shell (~869 LOC) + settings/* sections; only SectionId type still referenced by useTopMenuConfig.
hotspots.suggested_action: Move SectionId type out, then retire orphan SettingsPage; migrate unique Edge diagnostics sections into shared settings via SettingsPort.

hotspots.why: Near-fork of desktop TeamRunConsole (~999 LOC) with no product importer; only unit-tested.
hotspots.suggested_action: Do not merge blindly; extract shared TeamRun view model first or delete if product path is workbench/team pages.

hotspots.why: Desktop TeamRun console (~636 LOC) also appears unwired from current App/workbench shell.
hotspots.suggested_action: Inventory whether TeamRunDock/workbench routes supersede it; if yes, archive with tests preserved as shared behavior specs.

hotspots.why: Giant orchestrator (~1768 LOC) plus 2987-line test; ConversationHost extraction started but shell still too large.
hotspots.suggested_action: Continue extraction: routes/inspector/callbacks already partial; split state machine and keep behavior tests, not UI snapshot megatests.

hotspots.why: Giant router (~1404 LOC) owns settings/agents/projects pages wiring and is a blast radius for cleanup.
hotspots.suggested_action: Keep page components, thin route table; avoid moving product settings back to desktop/web.

hotspots.why: Canonical product dataMode contract; auto allows mock/fixture, enabling AH-SR-043 false-success paths if UI claims real execution.
hotspots.suggested_action: Keep contract, but force explicit badges and block production mutation claims unless observed/approved-real + auth evidence.

hotspots.why: Older alternate dataMode vocabulary (loading/live/offline-snapshot/mock) coexists with demo/dataMode.ts, increasing semantic drift.
hotspots.suggested_action: Deprecate or rename to catalog-source mode; stop exporting as if product dataMode.

hotspots.why: Implements AgentHubPlatform but defaults to mock, and non-mock hub failures silently fall back to fixtures.
hotspots.suggested_action: Fail closed in observed/approved-real; surface empty/error state instead of fixture success.

hotspots.why: Core renderer adapter (659 LOC) with oversized tests (adapter 1773 + pipeline 1361); healthy but costly to change.
hotspots.suggested_action: Preserve behavior; split tests by concern (grouping/order/tool-replace/markdown) before refactors.

super_scores.notes: Contract is clean and small. Gaps: conversations port underused by real models; SettingsPort optional and partially implemented; createMockPlatform is test-oriented only.
Strong pure normalizers + order + evidence. Diagnostic filter exists but narrow (runtimeDiagnostics patterns). High test coverage, large files.
Renderer pipeline healthy via ChatViewBridge. Giant adapter/tests reduce replaceability. Good separation from shell.
Owns product UI correctly, but AgentHubWorkbench/WorkbenchRoutes/RightInspector/useWorkbenchCallbacks are multi-concern giants; still imports mockData for fallbacks.
shared hubClient and queryKeys exist, but desktop/web still maintain parallel clients/stores; not yet SSOT.
Good Tauri/Edge host extensions, but demo defaults and model-layer data ownership bypass ConversationPort.
Web adapter correctly disables localEdge/localFiles; mutation/optimistic-cache logic is oversized for an adapter.
Many residual local UI/API forks from pre-shared era (Settings/TeamRun/components). Product shell improved; leftovers remain.
Same residual fork pattern as desktop; web SettingsPage is the worst single-file debt.
Boundary isolation is good. Platform contract partial; fixture fallback and separate UI stack keep it off Desktop/Web cleanup critical path.
Useful explicit demo/fixture system and dataMode contract, but imported into product adapters too broadly (AH-SR-043).

contradictions.topic: ConversationPort ownership vs actual conversation source
contradictions.sources: platform/types.ts ConversationPort; desktopPlatform/webPlatform conversations.list demo; useDesktopWorkbenchModel/useWebWorkbenchModel real session/thread lists
contradictions.impact: Adapter contract looks complete, but product conversation truth lives outside the port. Cleanup that assumes list() is SSOT will break UI.

contradictions.sources: shared workbench/pages/SettingsPage used by WorkbenchRoutes; desktop/web components/SettingsPage orphans; desktop settings sections + SettingsPort adapters
contradictions.impact: Three settings implementations create false 'active surface' assumptions. Safe cleanup must not migrate logic from orphans until import graph is proven dead.

contradictions.sources: desktop/web views/TeamRunConsole near-forks; desktop TeamRunDock; shared demo/teamrunDemo; no App-level TeamRunConsole import
contradictions.impact: Unclear whether TeamRun is product, demo, or dead. Merging forks before deciding product owner risks reviving dead UI.

contradictions.sources: demo/dataMode.ts (auto/mock/fixture/observed/approved-real) vs workbenchDataMode.ts (loading/live/offline-snapshot/mock/unavailable)
contradictions.impact: Agents and UI can mislabel real/mock state; test claims and AH-SR-043 evidence become ambiguous.

contradictions.sources: shared hubClient used by mobile; desktop/web each own full clients; method parity incomplete
contradictions.impact: Type/method drift (Session shapes, task approvals/artifacts, team APIs) can cause silent feature asymmetry across surfaces.

contradictions.sources: 04-frontend-data-flow forbids demo/mock in chat bubbles and requires platform isolation; desktop/web platforms still seed demo conversations and allow demoRuntimeFallback; mobile falls back to fixtures on hub error
contradictions.impact: False private-chat/execution success (AH-SR-043) remains plausible in auto/demo paths even with shared renderer health.

recommendations.action: Freeze architecture and inventory dead code before edits: mark desktop/web SettingsPage, TeamRunConsole, and duplicated pre-shared components as orphan candidates with import-graph evidence; do not delete in first PR without runtime smoke.
recommendations.rationale: Product path already uses shared workbench; residual forks are the main confusion/cost source.
recommendations.risk_if_skipped: Cleanup will keep editing dead forks or accidentally revive them.

recommendations.action: Make shared hubClient the SSOT and migrate desktop/web callers incrementally (types first, then methods, then delete forks). Keep surface-specific auth/token storage outside shared client.
recommendations.rationale: Triplicated hubClient is the largest divergence debt and blocks safe feature parity.
recommendations.risk_if_skipped: Desktop/Web/Mobile continue drifting APIs and bugfixes land only on one surface.

recommendations.action: Harden AH-SR-043 gates: production mutations require observed/approved-real + auth; demo/fixture only via explicit dataMode; badge/status always visible; mobile must not silent-fixture on hub failure.
recommendations.rationale: Security register still open; current auto/demo fallbacks can fake success.
recommendations.risk_if_skipped: False execution/private-chat claims remain; release evidence stays untrusted.

recommendations.action: Align platform adapter usage with contract: either populate ConversationPort from real models or stop pretending list() is product data; keep demo seeds out of default platform constructors.
recommendations.rationale: Current contract compliance is partial and misleading.
recommendations.risk_if_skipped: Future shared UI work will call wrong data source.

recommendations.action: Preserve transcript pipeline as-is during cleanup; only add missing diagnostic filters or parity tests. Split giant chatview/workbench tests by concern before behavioral refactors.
recommendations.rationale: Transcript health is relatively strong and product-critical.
recommendations.risk_if_skipped: Cleanup regressions will show as chat ordering/flicker bugs that are hard to diagnose.

recommendations.action: Continue workbench decomposition without changing product behavior: AgentHubWorkbench → already has ConversationHost/Routes/Inspector; next extract status/loading/agent-action state and shrink mega-tests.
recommendations.rationale: Giant shell/test files dominate change cost.
recommendations.risk_if_skipped: Every feature touches 1k+ LOC files and test runtime stays expensive.

recommendations.action: Resolve Settings ownership: shared SettingsPage remains product UI; desktop-only Edge diagnostics/settings move behind SettingsPort/host diagnostics; delete orphan desktop/web SettingsPage after extracting unique value.
recommendations.rationale: Avoid re-forking settings while recovering useful Edge-only sections.
recommendations.risk_if_skipped: Either lose Edge diagnostics or keep three settings UIs forever.

recommendations.action: Decide TeamRun product owner before merge: if still needed, extract shared TeamRun view model + console; if superseded by workbench/team pages, archive desktop/web consoles and keep tests as behavior specs.
recommendations.rationale: Near-duplicate consoles are unwired and costly.
recommendations.risk_if_skipped: Wasted merge work or accidental reintroduction of dead UI.

recommendations.action: Collapse residual desktop/web component forks that already have shared replacements (DiffViewer/Markdown/Approval/StatusBar etc.) only after verifying shared ui/workbench coverage; leave Desktop-only native chrome alone.
recommendations.rationale: Many same-named components still exist under desktop/web despite shared workbench path.
recommendations.risk_if_skipped: CSS/behavior drift continues in unused or partially used shells.

recommendations.action: Keep mobile boundary-only in this cleanup wave: fix fixture fail-closed and shared hubClient consumption, but do not force shared workbench UI onto RN yet.
recommendations.rationale: AGENTS.md prioritizes Desktop/Web UI; mobile isolation is intentional.
recommendations.risk_if_skipped: Cleanup scope explodes into a second product surface.

recommendations.action: Retire or rename legacy workbenchDataMode.ts so product dataMode has one vocabulary; keep e2eDataModeContract as evidence gate.
recommendations.rationale: Dual mode vocabularies undermine cleanup and test claims.
recommendations.risk_if_skipped: Agents and humans will continue misreporting real vs mock state.
